title: Draft enforced Pico-only delegation proposal
description: User explicitly approved a focused proposal on 2026-10-31: Pico-created Sesh child sessions and reviews use Pico rather than Codex or another harness. Ground supported Sesh agent-selection APIs and distinguish harness from model/provider and tool routing from unrestricted shell process isolation. Discuss enforcement tradeoffs with the human, create an isolated draft proposal PR, keep status draft, and do not implement. This is a slice of pico-3b8; the full delegation lifecycle remains separate.
notes: Draft PR https://github.com/markmals/pico/pull/4; branch pico-only-delegation, isolated worktree /Users/orion/Developer/Playgrounds/pico.pico-only-delegation. Human selected enforced Sesh start_session boundary with ordinary shell access retained, not OS process isolation. Draft proposal 0003 rejects every agent override before dispatch, omits agent for Sesh same-registration inheritance, preserves native-worker exclusion and prohibits shell-harness fallbacks in guidance. No implementation or global Sesh registration changes; live Pico child verification is an implementation requirement.
close_reason: Published proposal.0003 as a draft in PR #4; behavior and enforcement boundary selected with the human, 0 clarification markers, mise run check passed with 667 tests and 0 failures. No runtime implementation or live Pico child claim. Parent pico-3b8 remains open for broader delegation work.

title: Diagnose OMP cleanup approval prompts in Sesh
description: User reports recurring approval requests when OMP through Sesh runs rm -rf on agent-created /tmp files. Pico proposal.0001 already guarantees no approval requests. Diagnose the requesting layer from recorded metadata, OMP SDK and Sesh interfaces without rerunning destructive commands or changing global settings. Deliver an evidence-backed explanation and identify whether any Pico change is needed; no policy implementation in this task.
notes: Diagnosis completed from relevant Sesh session metadata/events and OMP 18.14.0 source, without re-running cleanup. Recorded rm -rf /tmp prompts were emitted in stock oh-my-pi/omp-acp sessions by the ACP critical-command gate; override decisions are per-call and not cached by Always allow. Pico does not expose requestPermission on WriteBridge and sets explicit yolo/autoApprove. A nonexecuting Bun probe used the real BashTool.approval and resolveApproval under loadPicoSettings: commandExecuted=false, approvalMode=yolo, decision override=true/reason Critical pattern detected, resolved policy=allow/override=false. This is resolver evidence, not a live Pico/Sesh cleanup run. No Pico policy change or global configuration change is needed for the observed stock-OMP prompts. Parent must actually run Pico to receive its policy.
close_reason: Diagnosed stock OMP ACP gate; verified Pico resolver behavior without executing cleanup. Findings recorded in proposal 0003 draft context and the Sesh conversation.

title: check-before-stop hook times out before mise run check can finish
description: The .omp/extensions/check-before-stop.ts harness hook gives mise run check 25 seconds, but the gate takes ~48 s on this Mac (649 tests plus macos:check with tuist/xcodebuild). Every turn end therefore reports 'mise run check did not finish within 25 seconds' and sends the agent back to rerun it by hand, though the gate passes. Expected: the hook waits long enough for the gate it enforces (or runs a scoped subset and says so). Found during proposal.0001 (PR #1); outside its scope.

title: Proposal: Pico Mac companion app
description: The native SwiftUI/AppKit configuration app described in PROTOTYPE.md (Native macOS configuration app) and VISION.md: providers and accounts, models, tools and integrations, Sesh setup, diagnostics; bundled runtime and helper (bun build --compile currently fails to embed OMP's pi_natives addon, spike 2026-10-30). Mark also wants Pico to connect to arbitrary MCP servers configured through this app (2026-10-30); proposal.0001 connects only the MCP servers Sesh sends. Sequenced after the adapter proposals.

title: Proposal: Sesh Autonomous support via a Pico-owned credential and state store
description: Sesh Autonomous sessions run the agent in a macOS sandbox whose embedded rules (strings in /opt/homebrew/opt/sesh/bin/seshd 0.25.2) allow writes only to the session folder, git data, temp, and a fixed list: .claude .codex .gemini .cursor .pi .local/state .npm .cache Library/Caches .bun .pnpm-store .yarn. ~/.omp is not on it. Under a sandbox-exec approximation (2026-10-30), OMP 18.14.0's discoverAuthStorage() and createAgentSession() fail: 'Database "/Users/orion/.omp/agent/agent.db": attempt to write a readonly database'. proposal.0001 (PR #1) uses the user's OMP store in place and fails Autonomous sessions with an explanatory error. Expected outcome of this proposal: Pico works in a real Sesh Autonomous session, with its credentials and state in a Pico-owned folder the sandbox allows (e.g. ~/.local/state/pico). It must decide how credentials get there (explicit import from OMP vs separate sign-in) and handle the risk that refreshing a copied rotating OAuth token signs terminal OMP out. Mark chose a separate proposal on 2026-10-30.

title: Proposal: delegation through Sesh child sessions
description: Follow-up to proposal.0001 (PR #1). 0001 exposes Sesh's mcp__sesh_* session tools because Sesh supplies them, but does not design or verify delegation. This proposal covers agent guidance for start/send/read/wait/stop, children running the same Pico agent with the curated policy (verify inheritance), distinguishing a child's completion, failure and waiting-for-user states, separate worktrees and explicit integration of child changes (PROTOTYPE.md criteria 8 and 9). OMP's native task tool stays permanently excluded (Mark, 2026-10-30).

title: Session load, list and resume for Pico
description: Persist Pico sessions in a Pico-owned directory and implement session/load (with replay), session/list and session/resume, so a Sesh restart can resume earlier conversations. Model and thinking-level selection moved into proposal 0001 (returned for revisions on 2026-10-30), so it is no longer part of this item.
